dedupe_keys.name: steer structural extreme events reconnaissance reports and datasets on designsafe

description: StEER, the Structural Extreme Events Reconnaissance network, documents how buildings and other structures perform in hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes and tsunamis, and publishes its reports and field data on the DesignSafe Data Depot with DOIs. Its products include preliminary virtual reconnaissance reports compiled within days from public sources, early access reconnaissance reports from field teams, and datasets such as damage assessments, street-level panoramic imagery and drone imagery. Examples found by the sweeps: the 2023 magnitude 7.8 Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence in Türkiye and Syria, Hurricanes Laura and Ida, a Nashville tornado, and a door-to-door survey after the EF4 tornado of 28 May 2019 in Leavenworth County, Kansas. A DataCite search on 2026-09-26 for StEER records from DesignSafe returned 115 results. Access: open download of each project from DesignSafe. Licence: set per project; several records state none in DataCite. Caveats: preliminary reports rely on media and social media and are superseded by field data; coverage follows where teams were deployed. Simulation uses are post-event damage observations for calibrating fragility models and studying recovery. Related records: the Hurricane Michael HAZUS validation data and the Türkiye earthquake damage datasets.
